title: Aruoba Term Structure of Inflation Expectations (ATSIX) — December 2026 update, 2:00 p.m. ET, the first read of the curve after the 12-09 FOMC and the 12-11 cliff
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 131,096 bytes) — the Philadelphia Fed's own release calendar, whose embedded structured data carries the row verbatim as {"title":"Aruoba Term Structure of Inflation Expectations","month":"december 2026","day":"29","displayMonth":"Dec","year":"2026","time":"2:00 p.m."}. The same payload's 2026-11-20 2:00 p.m. ATSIX row matches, byte for byte in its own field, the date the PIES lane independently proposed as aruoba-inflation-term-structure-2026-11-20 — an internal cross-check that this parse of the calendar is reading the feed correctly rather than a neighbouring row. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own release schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only). notes: PROPOSED (not canonical) by the livingston-survey-2026-12-11 initial-research adjacency sweep on 2026-09-09, from the same Philadelphia Fed calendar payload that dated its proposer. Filed as the NEXT edition of an instrument a sibling lane has already judged worth tracking: proposals/aruoba-inflation-term-structure-2026-11-20.from-philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25.json exists, so this is a cadence continuation, not a new call on whether the family belongs. What makes the December edition worth its own row rather than a footnote is position: ATSIX is a continuous curve of expected inflation from three to 120 months ahead, and the 12-29 update is the first one published AFTER the December FOMC (fomc-2026-12-09, high, confirmed), the December CPI (cpi-2026-12-10, high, confirmed) and the funding cliff (cr-expiry-2026-12-11, high, estimate) have all resolved — the exact opposite position from the proposer, whose own content is fixed at a 2026-10-31 base by the publisher's mailed-questionnaire rule and therefore cannot see any of them. It is also the only Philadelphia Fed instrument on this shelf that would let a later session ask whether the cliff moved the SHORT end of expectations while the Livingston panel's semiannual read could not. Whoever writes the canonical file owns (a) establishing the update cadence from an ATSIX-specific page rather than the shared calendar row — the 2026 calendar shows only 11-20 and 12-29, which is not obviously monthly and needs its own check — and (b) deciding whether a model-derived curve rather than a survey response earns a calendar entry at all; a DECLINE with the reasoning recorded is a perfectly good outcome. Impact LOW and symbols [] on the same grounds as every Philadelphia Fed entry on this shelf: no house playbook is macro-keyed and no tracked name carries an inflation-expectations channel. This is a PROPOSAL and an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the proposing ledger registers no forward test that depends on it.
